title: Kernel Thermostat: adaptive kernel rate-limiter for mixed seq-len workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight "thermostat" control in the runtime that limits how frequently we switch kernel implementations for a given request class. The goal is to reduce performance variance and kernel-switch thrash under mixed-sequence-length traffic while still allowing exploration and autotuning. This ticket covers design, probe instrumentation, a rollout plan, and benchmarks for the thermostat heuristic across heterogeneous GPU families.
acceptance_criteria: Thermostat module implemented in runtime with configuration knobs (window_size, max_switch_rate, hysteresis_factor).
Integration with existing kernel selector so per-request metadata (arch, seq_len_bucket, batch_profile) is considered before applying switch limits.
Lightweight probe mode that triggers controlled kernel switches and reports latency/cost deltas to tuning service.
End-to-end benchmarks showing >=15% reduction in p95 latency spikes for mixed seq-len workloads without >5% throughput regression on steady-state traffic for tested GPU families.
Feature flagged rollout with metrics and an automatic rollback rule if error or latency budgets are violated.
tasks: Design thermostat heuristic and edge cases (cold start, very-long-seq, burst traffic).
Add runtime counters/metrics for switch_count, switch_rejected_by_thermostat, average_seq_len_per_window.
Implement per-class rate limiter using exponential moving average window and hysteresis guards.
Wire probe scheduler to perform controlled exploration (1% traffic) with tagging for observed cost/latency.
Create perf harness and run benchmarks on A100, H100, and an older Ampere T4-like baseline.
Create console dashboard tiles for thermostat metrics and rollout health checks.
Document configuration knobs and recommended defaults in Confluence and runtime config reference.
Ship feature flag and coordinate canary rollout.
notes: Motivation: observed oscillation when selector explores faster than kernel warm-up / KV cache stabilization leading to p95 spikes.
Thermostat concept borrows ideas from networking token buckets + thermal throttling: allow baseline switches but cap frequency per class.
We must balance exploration (to find better kernels for new seq_len distributions) vs. stability (avoid repeated cold-path penalties).
Hysteresis is important: when a kernel switch improves latency by a margin X, increase the cooldown before allowing another switch for that class.
Evaluate interactions with batching: thermostat should consider effective per-token cost when batching increases/decreases.
